newsitem.title: UK: Allied Domecq limited exposure to Bass news.
newsitem.headline: Allied Domecq limited exposure to Bass news.

text.p: Allied Domecq Plc said on Friday its decision to have an unconditional sale of its brewing interests meant it had limited its exposure to the fallout from the UK government blocking the merger between Bass Plc and Carlsberg-Tetley.

Tony Hales, Allied Domecq chief executive, said "This (unconditional sale) has guaranteed our exit from brewing and limited our exposure to the subsequent uncertainties sourrounding Carlsberg-Tetley." Allied had agreed last August to sell its 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley to Bass for 200 million pounds under their merger plan.

Hales added in his statement "The disposal remains earnings enhancing under the fallback arrangements and has already met our strategic objective of enabling us to concentrate on our two core business streams."
Primarily, this included running its retailing arm as a specialist operation, developing its pub brand names, which include the Big Steak Pub, Wacky Warehouse and Firkin.
The statement followed the UK government's blocking of the proposed merger between Bass and Carlsberg-Tetley earlier on Friday.
